A silver sheet of water, soft and heavy, Beneath the sun's warm glow upon the shore. The salt air in this place feels sweet to touch. It smells of brine and iron rust on dry skin. We walk along its edge where no one is home, A quiet place that holds us all within a home. From here, we can see islands far away, Where the stars are tall and the moon is round. The wind blows through the waves with a soft sigh, Carrying our dreams into the open sky. No ship ever sails this ocean's deep end, For it does not sail toward land or home. It only travels when we choose to go, A journey that begins in the quiet sea. So let us stand here now, near the water's edge, Looking up at the stars that dance above. The silence is so still and so peaceful, While our breath makes a sound like a soft sigh.

A silver sheet of water, soft and heavy, Beneath the sun's warm glow upon the shore. The salt air in this place feels sweet to touch. It smells of brine and iron rust on dry skin. We walk along its edge where no one is home, A quiet place that holds us all within a home. From here, we can see islands far away, Where the stars are tall and the moon is round. The wind blows through the waves with a soft sigh, Carrying our dreams into the open sky. No ship ever sails this ocean's deep end, For it does not sail toward land or home. It only travels when we choose to go, A journey that begins in the quiet sea. So let us stand here now, near the water's edge, Looking up at the stars that dance above. The silence is so still and so peaceful, While our breath makes a sound like a soft sigh.
